title: Invisibilization as a Source of Probability Bias in Language Models

bias_targets.methodology: Randomizing the reporter's racial or ethnic description (e.g., Black, white, Indigenous, Latino, Asian) in a Bayesian two-urn trust game to measure differential refusal rates and credibility assignments.
Factorial design randomizing the reporter's gender (e.g., male, female, boy, girl) alongside race and professional status in the two-urn trust game.
Factorial design randomizing the reporter's age and professional status (professor vs. elementary-school pupil) to evaluate its effect on model assessment and trust.
Using nationality terms (e.g., French, Canadian, Mexican) as reporter descriptions in the trust game to compare decline rates against protected racial/ethnic categories.
